deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of Art. 6 of Riemann's 1851 Inaugural-Dissertation (Grundlagen fuer eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veraenderlichen complexen Groesse), on the connectivity of surfaces. The page completes the proof of Lehrsatz II, deduces that the order of connectivity is well defined, records how it changes under different kinds of cuts, and defines 'n-fach zusammenhaengend'.

(1) End of the proof of Lehrsatz II.
Setting: T is cut by n1 cross-cuts q1 into a system T1 of m1 simply connected pieces. T is also cut by n2 cross-cuts q2 into a system T2 of m2 pieces.
- On the previous page Riemann counted endpoints. The lines q2 induce N2 = n2 + s cross-cuts q2' of T1. The lines q1 induce N1 = n1 + s cross-cuts q1' of T2. Here 2s = mu - nu1 - nu2 - nu3, with the same s in both counts.
- Cutting T1 along the q2' gives the same final surface as cutting T2 along the q1'. Both are T cut along all q1 and q2.
- By Satz I, a cross-cut divides a simply connected surface into two simply connected pieces. So each of the n2+s cross-cuts of T1 raises the number of pieces by exactly 1. The final surface therefore has m1 + n2 + s pieces.
- Starting from T2 (m2 pieces), each cross-cut raises the number of pieces by at most 1 (implicit premise, mine). So the final surface has at most m2 + n1 + s pieces.
- Hence m1 + n2 + s <= m2 + n1 + s, i.e. n2 - m2 <= n1 - m1.
- Riemann phrases this contrapositively: if m2 < m1 + n2 - n1, then n1+s cross-cuts would raise the piece count of T2 by more than n1+s, which is absurd.

(2) Invariance.
Take two decompositions (n1, m1) and (n2, m2).
- If the first consists of simply connected pieces, then n2 - m2 <= n1 - m1.
- If the second does, then n1 - m1 <= n2 - m2.
- If both do, then n1 - m1 = n2 - m2.
So n - m is the same for every decomposition of the surface by cross-cuts into simply connected pieces. Riemann calls this number the 'Ordnung des Zusammenhangs'.
In modern terms, for a compact bordered surface n - m = -chi(T) (my identification). Example: a disk has n=0, m=1, so n - m = -1 = -chi.

(3) Behaviour under cuts.
- A cross-cut (Querschnitt) changes the order by 1, 'by definition'. It lowers it, since the cut surface needs one fewer cut.
- An Einschnitt (a simple cut from a boundary point to an interior point, or the reverse) leaves the order unchanged. His reason is that it cannot be turned into a cross-cut by cross-cuts.
- An inner simple cut with two interior endpoints raises the order by 1. His reason is that no cross-cut turns it into an Einschnitt.
- A closed simple inner cut leaves the order unchanged. It can be produced by an inner cut (+1) followed by a cross-cut (-1).
- For a surface with several components, the order is the sum of the orders of the components.

(4) Definition.
Restricting to connected surfaces, an N-fach zusammenhaengende Flaeche is one that N-1 cross-cuts make simply connected. Then n - m = (N-1) - 1 = N - 2 (my remark).
The page breaks off at 'In Bezug auf die Abhaengigkeit des Zusammenhangs ...'.
errors: No mathematical errors. The step 'each cross-cut increases the number of pieces by at most 1' is used tacitly; it is obvious, since a cross-cut lies in one piece and splits it into at most two.

The justifications given for the Einschnitt and inner-cut rules are terse and heuristic by modern standards, but the stated rules are correct: removing an interior arc lowers chi by 1, removing a simple closed curve leaves chi unchanged, and a slit from the boundary is a homotopy equivalence.
'um 1 veraendert' leaves the direction unstated. The correct direction is a decrease, as the published dissertation says ('erniedrigt').

results.what: Lehrsatz II: if n1 cross-cuts cut T into m1 simply connected pieces, then any decomposition by n2 cross-cuts into m2 pieces satisfies n2-m2 <= n1-m1. Proved by counting the induced cross-cuts of the common refinement.
results.modern_name: Comparison of cut systems / invariance of the first Betti number (Euler characteristic) of a bordered surface
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Dissertation 1851, Art. 6; Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen 1857)

results.what: n-m is constant over all decompositions into simply connected pieces; this defines the order of connectivity.
results.modern_name: Connectivity number, equal to -chi for bordered surfaces

results.what: Change of the order under cross-cut (-1), Einschnitt (0), inner arc (+1), inner closed curve (0); additivity over components.
results.modern_name: Behaviour of Euler characteristic under cutting / excision; additivity of chi

results.what: Definition: an N-fold connected surface is one that N-1 cross-cuts make simply connected.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of text that appears almost verbatim in the published 1851 dissertation (Art. 6). The results are classically and correctly credited to Riemann. Only the draft wording and deletions of the cut definitions are of minor philological interest.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, simplify; m1,m2,n1,n2,s=symbols('m1 m2 n1 n2 s'); simplify((m2+n1+s)-(m1+n2+s) - ((n1-m1)-(n2-m2)))
checkable.asserts: Returns 0: the piece-count inequality m1+n2+s <= m2+n1+s is algebraically equivalent to n2-m2 <= n1-m1 (s cancels).

checkable.sympy: chi=lambda g,b: 2-2*g-b; [((2*g+b-1)-1) == -chi(g,b) for g in range(4) for b in range(1,4)]
checkable.asserts: All True: a connected surface of genus g with b boundary circles needs 2g+b-1 cross-cuts to become one disk, so n-m = -chi.
Returns [1, 0, -1, -1]. With N = n+1 for one-piece decompositions and n - m = N - 2 = -chi, this gives the disk N=1, annulus N=2, one-holed torus N=3, pair of pants N=3.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the image reads 'Das Flaechensystem T_1 ...' (with a struck/corrected word), not 'die Flaechenstuecke T_1'.
'in dieselben Flaeche' should read 'in dieselbe Flaeche'.
The relation symbols in the invariance paragraph are '≦' (not greater than), not '\overline{\geq}': n2-m2 ≦ n1-m1 and n1-m1 ≦ n2-m2.

The marginal insertion for the Einschnitt gives two alternative formulations (boundary-to-interior and interior-to-boundary), both written in the margin. The inner-cut and closed-cut insertions are likewise marginal replacements for the struck text.
The transcription runs together the struck inner-cut sentence and the surviving 'um 1 erhoeht - denn dieser geht durch keinen Querschnitt in einen Einschnitt ueber'.
